story.title: US Suggests Ukraine Consider Territorial Cession for NATO Membership, Says Zelenskyy
story.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that the United States has proposed the idea of Ukraine ceding parts of the Donbas region to Russia as a condition for joining NATO. This marks the first time the US has raised the possibility of territorial concessions in exchange for NATO membership. Zelenskyy indicated that discussions are ongoing regarding specific security guarantees from Western allies.

explore_lenses.label: What territory is at issue, and who decides?
explore_lenses.title: A withdrawal would concern Ukrainian-held Donbas
explore_lenses.summary: The reported U.S. question concerned whether Ukraine would withdraw from parts of Donbas that remain under Kyiv’s control, rather than recognition that Russia lawfully owns the territory. Any formal territorial change would face both Ukrainian constitutional requirements and the UN-backed position on Ukraine’s internationally recognized borders.

claims.text: Zelenskyy said the U.S. asked whether Ukraine would withdraw from Donbas if it joined NATO; reporting specifies this referred to areas of Donbas Russia does not control.
Ukraine still holds about one-fifth of Donetsk, including a defensive network described as strategically important by Sky News.
Ukraine’s constitution says its territory within its existing borders is integral and inviolable, and that changes to Ukraine’s territory are decided exclusively by an all-Ukrainian referendum.

The UN General Assembly has reaffirmed Ukraine’s territorial integrity within its internationally recognized borders and called Russia’s asserted changes to the status of parts of Donetsk and other regions inconsistent with the UN Charter.

explore_lenses.label: Would a NATO pledge make this a settled deal?
explore_lenses.title: NATO membership is not yet assured
explore_lenses.summary: A U.S. exploratory question is not itself a NATO accession guarantee. Admission requires unanimous approval by NATO allies, and the alliance’s secretary general said in June that unanimity for Ukraine’s full membership did not exist at that time.

claims.text: NATO says invitations to join are decided by consensus of all allies in the North Atlantic Council; no outside country can decide the matter.
NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte said on June 3, 2026 that Ukraine’s path was described as irreversible but that there was not then unanimity among allies for full membership.

Zelenskyy said Kyiv was discussing a broader package of specific NATO and EU security guarantees, a strong military, financial support and recovery assistance; he said he would ask Ukrainian society whether to accept terms if partners confirmed them.
Zelenskyy’s stated position is that an arrangement need not recognize occupied territory as Russian, even if it involved a withdrawal or other territorial arrangement.

explore_lenses.label: What diplomatic steps are actually next?
explore_lenses.title: Negotiations continue without a breakthrough
explore_lenses.summary: The immediate process remains open-ended: the Abu Dhabi talks produced no reported settlement, while participants agreed that Europeans should be included in future negotiations. Security guarantees, a possible energy ceasefire and the role of European forces remain unresolved issues.

claims.text: The November 10 Abu Dhabi coordination meeting included the EU, France, Germany, Italy, the United Kingdom, Ukraine, the United States and NATO; their joint statement said they were coordinating on ending the war and on robust security guarantees as part of any settlement.
Reporting on the subsequent Abu Dhabi discussions said they ended without a breakthrough, but with agreement that European officials would be included in future negotiations.
Zelenskyy said Russia rejected a proposed ceasefire on attacks against energy targets; this is his account of the talks, not a jointly announced agreement.

Putin said any post-ceasefire deployment of European troops in Ukraine would be unacceptable and would be treated by Russia as a security threat, according to AP’s report on his remarks to U.S. envoys.

story_report.summary: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the United States had asked whether Ukraine would withdraw from parts of the Donbas still under Kyiv’s control in exchange for joining NATO, the first time Washington had raised such an option, according to his account. The proposal has not produced an announced agreement: Kyiv is continuing discussions with Western partners over security guarantees, military strength, financial support and recovery assistance. NATO membership, meanwhile, would require unanimous approval by all allies rather than a decision by Washington alone.

sections.heading: Donbas Withdrawal Raises Legal Questions
sections.body: The reported question concerned Donbas areas Russia does not control. Ukraine still holds about one-fifth of Donetsk, including a defensive network Sky News described as strategically important. Ukraine’s constitution defines its territory within existing borders as integral and inviolable, and says territorial changes can be decided only through an all-Ukrainian referendum. The UN General Assembly has also reaffirmed Ukraine’s territorial integrity within its internationally recognized borders and rejected Russia’s asserted status changes in occupied regions as inconsistent with the UN Charter.

sections.heading: NATO Membership Requires Allied Consensus
sections.body: NATO says invitations are decided by consensus in the North Atlantic Council, and no outside country can determine the outcome. Secretary General Mark Rutte said in June that Ukraine’s path toward NATO had been described as irreversible, but that allies did not then have unanimity for full membership. Zelenskyy has said any arrangement need not recognize occupied territory as Russian, even if it involved a withdrawal or another territorial arrangement; he said he would ask Ukrainian society whether to accept terms confirmed by partners.

sections.heading: Abu Dhabi Talks Continue Without Breakthrough
sections.body: A November 10 coordination meeting in Abu Dhabi brought together the EU, France, Germany, Italy, the United Kingdom, Ukraine, the United States and NATO. Their joint statement said participants were coordinating on ending the war and building robust security guarantees as part of any settlement. Subsequent discussions ended without a breakthrough, though reporting said European officials would take part in future negotiations. Zelenskyy said Russia rejected a proposed halt to attacks on energy targets, while Vladimir Putin said European troop deployments after a ceasefire would be unacceptable to Moscow.

related_stories.title: Nationwide Flight Ground Stop in the US Due to Equipment Overload
related_stories.summary: On Friday, the Federal Aviation Administration implemented a nationwide ground stop, resulting in over 8,200 flight cancellations, which accounted for more than 31% of scheduled flights in the US. The ground stop lasted nearly five hours, marking the longest such event since September 11, 2001. Officials attributed the disruption to outdated air traffic communications equipment and confirmed there was no evidence of a cyber attack. Flights have since resumed as airspace reopened.

related_stories.title: Trump, Xi, and Putin to Hold Historic Meeting at APEC Summit in China
related_stories.summary: The leaders of the United States, China, and Russia are set to hold an unprecedented trilateral meeting on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, China. This meeting marks the first formal gathering of the three leaders, with discussions expected to focus on nuclear weapons reduction. The meeting is scheduled for next week.
